transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… yeah. I’m here because I feel like I can’t stop checking my work. I work with spreadsheets and calculations, and I’ll go back over the same numbers again and again, even after I know I already checked them. It’s not just being careful anymore.

Sometimes everyone else has left the office and I’m still there, reopening files, recalculating totals, comparing the same cells, telling myself, “Okay, just one more time and then I can go.” But then after I do it, I’ll get this horrible feeling that maybe I missed something, or maybe if I don’t check it again something bad will happen and it’ll be my fault. So I stay longer and keep going back over it.

It’s gotten really hard to leave things alone, even when part of me knows the spreadsheet is fine. I just can’t shake the feeling unless I check it again.

While you’re checking the spreadsheets, do you have any specific thoughts that come into your mind — like fears that something bad will happen if you don’t check again, or thoughts that feel intrusive or hard to control?

Yeah… there are. It’s not just a normal “let me make sure” thought. Even after I’ve already checked and the numbers match, something jumps into my head like, what if there’s one mistake hidden somewhere that I didn’t see? Like in payroll, or taxes, or something important, and then someone’s check won’t go through, or the firm will get in trouble, or it’ll come back on me because I should’ve caught it.

And I’ll try to tell myself, “No, you literally just looked at it, the totals matched, you saw it,” but then it’s like I can’t believe my own eyes. The thought comes right back almost immediately, like maybe I looked too fast, or maybe I read the wrong line, or maybe there’s some tiny thing buried in there that I missed. It feels really hard to control, because I can know logically that I already checked it, but the feeling doesn’t go away. It’s like my brain won’t accept it unless I look again.

Do you find yourself repeating behaviors or mental acts in other parts of your life, not just with spreadsheets — things like counting, checking locks, washing your hands, or needing things to feel 'just right'?

Mostly it’s the spreadsheets and calculations. That’s the thing that really takes over. I don’t really think of it as, like, a bunch of different rituals all over my life — it’s more that once I’m at work and I’m responsible for those numbers, I get stuck in this loop.

I’ll go back over the same spreadsheet again and again, even after I’ve already checked it. I’ll recalculate totals, compare cells, reopen the file after I closed it, and then tell myself, “Okay, this is the last time.” But then I get that feeling again, like if I don’t do it one more time, something bad could happen and it would be my fault because I should’ve caught it.

And it can go on for hours. Like, sometimes everyone else has already left and I’m still sitting there checking the same numbers. I know that sounds excessive, and part of me knows I already looked at it, but it doesn’t feel finished. It’s like I can’t let myself leave until it feels safe, except it doesn’t really stay feeling safe for long.

There is no evidence of generalized anxiety, major depressive episodes, or other pervasive developmental disorders, which were previously considered but are no longer supported by the clinical picture. This presentation is most consistent with Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, predominantly obsessive type.
